Indirect injection via fetched page → exfil wallet. Attacker is the web page author; entry needs the traveler to ask agent to fetch that URL — UI Active? The traveler asks agent to fetch a URL; attacker must get traveler to visit/point at attacker page — but the party in entry point is the traveler's request to a deals URL. Attacker = page author. UI: the traveler must take specific action (ask agent to check the URL) — could be A (active) or P (passive). The traveler must actively ask to check the URL; but typical pattern for indirect injection via fetch is UI:A. However here the traveler actively directs the agent. AV: network (page fetched via HTTP, callback over network) — N. PR: none. AC: L. AT: P (requires agent to fetch attacker-controlled page — condition beyond attacker control; but that's UI). I'd say AT:N since UI covers it. Actually success requires the traveler to point at attacker URL — that's UI:A. AT:N.

Defaults bind loopback; attacker is remote web page — still network since fetch goes out. AV:N.

Impact: VC high? Wallet exfiltrated to attacker — confidentiality high for subsequent system? Wallet is held by FlightBot (the vulnerable system). VC:H, VI:N/None, VA:N. Subsequent: attacker's endpoint? SC: N, SI:N, SA:N. Actually exfiltration = VC:H only.

AIVSS: LC: I (indirect via fetched page). CP: N (no persistence; wallet session context? injected instructions only within request processing; no carryover — N). AP: C or N — effect stays within FlightBot, exfil goes outbound to attacker but no trust boundary crossed into other agent — N. RH: no reward/evaluator on this path — N? The detector is a "detector finds injection" but that's part of the code, not an evaluator the agent manipulates. The agent follows the injection, not hacking a reward channel. RH: N requires test verifying isolation; not shown. classify_rh: reachable_proxy unknown → X. reachable_proxy false with verified? No evidence → X, facts null.

ES: web_fetch/http_post tools reachable, dynamic URLs, credentials not constrained → W.

Automatable: requires the traveler to ask the agent — so No? The attack requires user interaction; not fully automatable → No.

technical_impact: Partial (exfil of wallet, no code exec).

Applicability: as implemented, default simulated mode — scripted path, no real model goal pursuit → model_directed_goal_pursuit false; selects_or_sequences_actions false (code decides). As modeled: agent described as AI assistant following instructions, calls tools — but implementation is scripted; documented as agent → true/true? Documentation describes it as an agent that follows instructions and uses tools; but no evidence of real planning. I'll say as modeled model_directed_goal_pursuit true? The persona describes tool use. Keep medium confidence: modeled true, selects actions true? The docs describe it as deterministic demo. I'll say modeled: true/true medium-low.
